context:
Add `except BaseException: _kill_process_group(proc); raise` to the
communicate() try-block so cancellation reaps the group before unwinding.
Give the timeout_s==0 branch the same Popen+setsid+guarded-kill treatment.
Add a module-level registry of live child pgids drained by the orchestrator's
cancel path, covering the window between Popen and communicate.
Deliberately NOT changing the SIGTERM->SweepCancelled design: the durability
contract in cells_io.py depends on the KeyboardInterrupt unwinding path.
description:
tests/uat/timeouts.py::run_with_timeout kills the child process group ONLY inside
`except subprocess.TimeoutExpired`. There is no `finally` and no BaseException
handler. tests/uat/orchestrator.py converts a sweep SIGTERM into SweepCancelled,
which subclasses KeyboardInterrupt -- a BaseException. It therefore propagates
straight out of proc.communicate() with the child untouched.

Because run_with_timeout passes preexec_fn=os.setsid, the child is in its OWN
session, so it does not inherit the terminal's Ctrl-C either. The child is fully
orphaned.

OBSERVED 2026-08-04 (twice, stage 1 release-gate chunking): after killing the
sweep orchestrator, `benchbox run` and its Spark JVM survived 14+ minutes,
holding CPU, RAM and disk, and required manual SIGKILL. This is what made disk
exhaustion unrecoverable without operator intervention.

Second, narrower defect: the `timeout_s == 0` branch uses bare subprocess.run
with NO setsid and NO teardown path at all, so it leaks differently.

anti_patterns.instead: catch BaseException, kill the group, and re-raise unchanged
anti_patterns.why: SweepCancelled inherits KeyboardInterrupt, which is NOT an Exception -- an `except Exception` clause never fires and the bug survives the fix

anti_patterns.dont: claim this fixed without a test that actually spawns and cancels a real child
anti_patterns.instead: spawn a real sleeper, cancel, and assert no surviving descendant
anti_patterns.why: the whole defect is that a mocked communicate() looks correct while a real process survives

anti_patterns.dont: drop preexec_fn=os.setsid to make the child inherit terminal signals
anti_patterns.instead: keep setsid and make every exit path kill the group
anti_patterns.why: the session is what makes group-kill reliable for JVM and container child trees; removing it trades one leak for a worse one

anti_patterns.dont: swallow the cancellation after killing the group
anti_patterns.why: the sweep must still unwind so the platform teardown and finalize markers run

preserves.behavior: SweepCancelled stays a KeyboardInterrupt subclass; the cells_io durability contract (.inprogress/.finalized markers, per-cell fsync) is unchanged.
The SIGTERM handler is still installed only in the sweep's own main thread and restored on exit.
Timeout classification is unchanged: a per-cell timeout still returns EXIT_TIMEOUT=124 with timed_out=True.
Windows behavior is unchanged: no os.killpg, no setsid, proc.kill() fallback still applies.

prior_art.concept: install/restore SIGTERM shim (uat-sweep-durability-and-signal-teardown w2/w3) is the cancellation entry point; hook pgid draining there
existing killpg coverage stubs os.killpg and asserts the ladder; same stubbing technique applies to the BaseException path
_kill_process_group already implements the SIGTERM->200ms->SIGKILL ladder with hasattr(os,'killpg') portability guard; reuse it verbatim, only widen who calls it

verifications.expected: spawns a real long-running cell, SIGTERMs the sweep, asserts the child pgid is gone
